messages.text: For the short strips, I would actually prefer a barrel layout with phi-tilted modules (as in the original odd or ATLAS strips) - which would make the detector more symmetrical in phi. Make an alternative layout along that lines.

I’ll add a phi-tilted barrel alternative alongside the current straight-stave proposal, then compare placement, coverage and mechanical/service clearances. I’ll check the ODD and ATLAS conventions so the tilt direction and sensor axes are explicit.

I’m using the acts-spack workflow for the native checks. Its recorded setup and lockfile fingerprints have changed, so I’ll re-verify the installed runtime before relying on it.

I’ll keep the tangential layout as a control and add the tilted alternative to draft PR #49.

The native runtime is verified. The useful change is to put every stave in a layer at the same radius and give each the same phi tilt; that removes the alternating radial lanes and makes the geometry repeat at every stave pitch. I’ll rotate the cold plate, cooling and buses with the sensors, and check clearance for the full assembly before selecting the angle.

The first 15° candidate has 44/56/80/108 staves and 8,064 modules. The fine coordinate follows the tilted stave across phi, while the second coordinate stays along z. I’ve also added beveled ring feet so the tilted cold plate can meet the cylindrical support rings. Native checks will test those feet, neighbouring staves and end boards.

The 15° layout passed DD4hep construction with zero reported overlaps at the existing 10⁻⁵ mm tolerance. The 12° control failed with 602 flex-to-bus overlaps; 18° also passed, so I recommend 15° as the smallest angle tested. The straight layout still passes its checks, and its placements match the retained control exactly. Coverage and saved Geant4-hit checks are still running.

The refined coverage sample found substantially fewer boundary misses: 225 straight, 210 positive-charge and 174 negative-charge crossings, versus 1,311/1,132/1,135 for the tangential control. Both use the same denominator and sampling assumptions. There are no misses more than 100 mm from a nominal barrel end, though the remaining misses still need an endcap transition solution.

ROOT persistence and the Geant4 smoke check passed, with saved hits in all four layers. I’ll add the comparison drawing and report to PR #49, keeping the unresolved engineering limits visible.

The before/after drawing is ready. During the mounting review, I caught a detail worth correcting: the tilted feet should attach to a free CFRP land beside the backside buses. I’m checking that placement before publishing the alternative.

The final mounting web fits the free land between the insulation and signal bus, and the revised 15° assembly again passed with zero reported overlaps. The left-side shoe I tried crossed neighbouring cold plates; that rejected result is retained. The angle comparison is unchanged: 12° still has 602 flex/bus overlaps, while 15° and 18° pass.

I’m finishing the refreshed evidence and publishing the alternative to draft PR #49.

The alternative and before/after drawing are now pushed to [PR #49](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/49). The final native, persistence, transport and regression checks passed. It remains a draft: the narrower mounting web needs mechanical qualification, and the remaining barrel-end coverage and service limits are documented.

I’m checking the hosted build and closing out the session log.

The session log includes the rejected angle and mounting attempts alongside the final results, and both checkout logs validate. The hosted build is running on the published scientific commit. Current-turn token counters remain explicitly unknown because the turn is still active.

The hosted build failed. I’ll inspect the failed step and fix it before handing over the PR. The local native and transport checks passed; I’ll keep the CI result separate until I know what caused it.

The failure is in my new snapshot test: it compares floating-point values bit for bit, and Linux produced a last-digit difference from the macOS snapshot. I’ll keep identifiers and structure exact, allow only machine-scale rounding differences in floats, and add a check that rejects a real placement shift. The native overlap and engineering limits stay unchanged.

The corrected regression test has passed on Linux. The hosted build is now running the final documentation and dashboard checks; the geometry, inputs and retained native evidence are unchanged by the test fix.

The corrected hosted build passed. I’m making the final documentation and logging commit, then syncing the paired journal to the primary checkout. The 15° alternative and its scientific evidence are complete; PR #49 stays in draft for review.

Added the **15° phi-tilted alternative** to [PR #49](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/49):

- One stave radius per layer, with modules, support, cooling and buses rotating together.
- **288 staves / 8,064 modules**, preserving the sensor coordinates and barrel bounds.
- 15° is the smallest tested angle that clears the full assembly; 12° collided.

Native, ROOT persistence, Geant4 and Linux CI checks passed. End-transition coverage and mounting/service qualification remain open. The final documentation CI is running; the PR remains draft.
